title: A pane hosts any app — Pane, content components, and the scene seam that makes Terminal a widget
summary: The scrolling area hosts panes of any content — terminal, browser, neovim, agent — each a reusable component placeable anywhere, not a GPU pass welded to a pane.
description:
Decided by Antonio, 2026-08-18, in discussion. This phase is the record.

═══ THE ARCHITECTURE ═══

    Scrolling area (generic container of panes, in splittable columns)
      └─ Pane  — letter, zoom/float/split/remove, and the bounds it was given
           └─ Flex
                ├─ header (fixed)      ← the CONTENT's, absent for Neovim
                └─ ScrollRegion        ← the CONTENT scrolls, not the pane
                     └─ Terminal

Antonio: "the only responsibility of the pane is to draw the key hint letter, zoom in/out,
float/unfloat, split/unsplit, remove". And: "Terminal should be a reusable component similar to a
DOM <terminal/> we can put in any container in the app, even in a plugin or in a sidebar."

All content components implement one common trait so any of them can sit in a pane; a plugin author
can build a pane and use these components.

═══ THE CODE, AS IT SHOULD READ ═══

The terminal's own composition — heca/src/chrome/terminal/mod.rs, the ONLY file here that may
touch AppState:

    Flex::column()
        .gap_spacing(Spacing::Sm)
        .child(TerminalHeader { pane_id, info, buttons, shortcuts, cb }.build())
        .child(ScrollRegion::new()
            .child(Terminal { pane_id, surface, cb }.build()))

The pane shell — heca/src/chrome/pane/mod.rs. It composes the grid-ui `Pane` widget for its frame,
carries its own identity and letter, and holds exactly ONE content child:

    apply_pane_frame(Pane::new(), appearance.effective_pane_border_style())
        .key(pane_key(id))                      // identity — never an index
        .hint_placement(HintPlacement::Center)   // the letter sits centred over the pane
        .on_hint(fires(focus_pane(id), emit))    // what picking it does
        .child_boxed(content)                    // Terminal, Browser, Neovim, Agent, a plugin's

FIVE SPELLING RULES, each one a real trap:
1. `Flex::column()` / `Flex::row()` — there is no `Flex::new(child)`. And never name a UI box
   `Column`: `Column` already means a column of panes in heca-core.
2. `.gap_spacing(Spacing::Sm)` over `.gap(10.0)`. Both exist and both stay; the token is resolved
   from the inherited font at layout, so it scales with font, size variant and UI zoom. A raw px gap
   is tuned for one font size and wrong at every other — use it only when you can say why the number
   should not move with the font. Same for `.pad_all/.pad_x/.pad_y(Spacing)` vs `.padding(px)`.
3. Properties are STRUCT FIELDS and the constructor is a struct literal (AGENTS.md § 0b-bis rule 2).
   Not `Header::new(title, icon, buttons, active, cb)` — providers/workspaces/pane_card() at eleven
   positional arguments is the counter-example nobody can read.
4. `Terminal` has NO title and NO icon. Those are the header's facts. A terminal takes what it needs
   to draw its content and nothing more — which is exactly what lets it mount in a sidebar, where
   there is no title.
5. The icon buttons are NOT hand-listed. They come from the dynamic vector `pane_header_buttons`,
   which is what makes config-added, config-hidden and future plugin-added buttons work with no
   change here. Do not re-introduce a per-action match in a render loop.

═══ THE FOLDER STRUCTURE ═══

Per AGENTS.md § 0b-bis. heca/src/chrome/expose/ is the worked example to copy — 7 files including
testing.rs (mod.rs 733, model.rs 282, expose_grid.rs 327, workspace_row.rs 374, column_card.rs 149,
pane_card.rs 433, testing.rs 119).

    heca/src/chrome/
      pane/
        mod.rs            host wiring — the ONLY file that may touch AppState
        model.rs          the session reduced to plain data (id, rect, active, zoomed, floating)
        pane.rs           the shell component: frame + key + letter + one content child
        testing.rs        #[cfg(test)] fixtures
      terminal/
        mod.rs            host wiring — the ONLY file that may touch AppState
        model.rs          PaneInfoView and friends, reduced from the session
        terminal.rs       the <Terminal/> component
        terminal_header.rs the info bar: content segments + pane-action buttons
        testing.rs
      browser/            later — same shape
      neovim/             later — same shape, and NO header
      agent/              later — same shape

RULES THAT COME WITH THE SHAPE:
- mod.rs is the only file that may see AppState. Everything below it takes plain data and is
  testable headless.
- The seams travel as ONE group — a single callbacks struct built once and passed by reference, not
  threaded one argument at a time (expose::ExposeCallbacks is the pattern).
- Return the CONCRETE widget when the parent still has to size it; box only at the top.
- Sizes are shares (Length::Pct of one denominator, or a grow weight). Never a model number times a
  scale of your own.
- One headless test per component, plus the box test: lay it out in a box and assert it never
  exceeds it.
- It moves to heca/src/components/ only when a SECOND surface needs it — a move, never a copy. That
  folder is an empty shell today (mod.rs only).

═══ THE WIDGETS THIS IS BUILT FROM (all documented in docs/widgets.md) ═══
- `Pane` (heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/pane.rs) — the frame, three modes via PaneFrame:
  frameless/bordered/bracketed. Width, radius and colour from the theme and [appearance.pane].
  Applied through crate::chrome::apply_pane_frame.
- `Flex` — the arrangement; `.gap_spacing`, `.pad_*`, `.grow`, `.align`. No StyleExt on it by design.
- `ScrollRegion` — the viewport the content scrolls inside. Owns wheel, thumb drag, click-in-track
  paging, ensure_visible and the eight Scroll* WidgetIntents. Binds keyboard_target so only the
  focused region answers scroll keys.
- `IconButton` (+ `WidgetSize::Header`) and `Tooltip` — the header buttons; tip and shortcut derived
  from the action NAME via action_tooltip + ActionShortcuts, never a literal shortcut string.
- `Tag` (multi-segment), `Icon`, `Label`, `BadgeButton` — the header's content and the "N lines
  above" chip.
- The hint machinery: `Base::hint` / `hint_label` / `hint_style`, `HintPlacement::Center`,
  `component::paint_child` (which DRAWS the letter — a widget painted directly can never show one),
  `collect_hints` / `fire_hint` / `offer_hint`, `DEFAULT_LETTERS` (52, home row first),
  `KeyHintGroup` for a surface-scoped picker, and `paint_keycap`/`keycap_size` as the only sanctioned
  way to stamp a cap over something that is not a widget.
- `ComponentExt` — `.key(..)`, `.hintable(bool)`, and every handler. `Base::activatable` is what makes
  something pickable; `.hintable(false)` opts out.
- `FocusScope` — if a pane's content needs to be a keyboard area rather than a control.
- `Spacing` / `WidgetSize` tokens — the semantic sizes; the caller picks a variant, the widget owns
  the pixels.

═══ WHAT THE PANE DOES NOT DO ═══
It never computes its own geometry. Zoom, float, split, remove are performed by heca-core/src/layout/
(Session / ScrollingSpace / Column) via handlers in heca/src/handlers.rs reached through
ActionRegistry. The pane ASKS (dispatches the action), the core DOES, the renderer draws the new
rects. taffy never positions panes (AGENTS.md).

Buttons in the header simply dispatch actions, so they are not coupling — the same action is
reachable from a keybinding, the command palette and RPC. That is the documented chrome-button
pattern (name the action, never the styling).

═══ ALREADY TRUE (verified 2026-08-18) ═══
- heca-core's Pane (heca-core/src/layout/column.rs:392) is content-blind: id, title, custom_name,
  runtime, close_policy, preferred_height, animations. Its doc already says it "wraps the actual
  content (terminal, neovim, browser)".
- ScrollingSpace / Column (heca-core/src/layout/scrolling.rs, column.rs) know nothing about terminals.
- PaneBackend (heca-core/src/backend/mod.rs:187) is the process/IO seam, with terminal + fake impls.
- config already splits the info bar along this exact line (heca-config/src/appearance.rs):
  PaneSegment (Location/AppName/GitBranch/GitStatus) = content facts; PaneAction
  (Split/MoveLeft/MoveRight/Close) = pane actions.

═══ NOT TRUE YET — THE FILES THAT CHANGE ═══
- heca/src/app/terminal_render.rs (1700 lines) — paint_terminal_pane_shell:718 builds a grid-ui Pane
  fresh each frame and paints it with a DIRECT pane.paint(cx):783; the header is painted directly at
  :800; title_bar_reserve:626 / pane_title_top_inset:646 reserve the header's height on the pane;
  stable_tiled_content_rect:654 / stable_floating_content_rect:670 / pane_content_rect:903 compute
  the content rect by hand; sync_retained_terminal_layers:46, render_terminal_layer_update:399 and
  blit_retained_terminal_layer:294 are the GPU half that must be preserved.
- heca/src/app/render.rs — calls the shell from TWO sites, :691 (tiled) and :902 (floating); the
  48px host letter pass is at :951 (~43 lines, including a second loop for floats).
- heca/src/chrome/pane_header.rs (1086 lines) — sync_pane_headers:952 builds the retained per-pane
  bar; build_pane_info_bar:159; pane_info_view:76. state.pane_headers (app_state.rs:710) and
  state.pane_viewport_widgets (app_state.rs:725) are the two retained per-pane stores.
- heca/src/chrome/hint.rs — active_hint_targets:534 (the surface stack, layers → chrome → panes),
  offer_hint_letters:356, target_identity:321, fire_hint, clear_hint_letters. HintSurface::
  PaneHeader(pane_id) becomes the pane.
- heca/src/handlers.rs — handle_pane_select:776 (index-based, the defect), assign_letters:816 (pure,
  already correct, serves both pickers), handle_hint_pick:845.
- heca/src/app/selection.rs — collect_all_pane_candidates:41 is pure index; PANE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT:9
  and candidate_letter:17 already read DEFAULT_LETTERS.
- heca/src/mouse/hit_test.rs:17 — hand-written pane hit test with a hardcoded 40.0 sidebar width.
  mouse/ is 2644 lines across target.rs, drag.rs, release.rs, interactive.rs, resize.rs.
- heca-grid-ui/src/scene.rs — ⚠️ THE ENABLING GAP: DrawCommand is ONLY Rect / Brackets / Text /
  Scanline / PushClip / PopClip. AGENTS.md lists `Custom` and `Gradient` — BOTH ARE STALE, neither
  exists. Fix that line in AGENTS.md as part of this phase.
- No PaneKind enum anywhere. AGENTS.md specifies SpawnPane { kind, program, argv, float, width,
  height } with terminal|browser|nvim_gui as the target shape; nothing implements it.

═══ THE KEY DESIGN CALL ═══
Both content kinds collapse to ONE shape: the pane's content child is ALWAYS a component. For a
browser/agent/plugin it is a real tree (Flex, Grid, ScrollRegion). For the terminal it is a leaf
that paints one new scene command naming an externally-rendered surface + its rect; the renderer maps
that id to the texture it already blits. The library stays GPU-free — same split Text already has
(the scene says what, the renderer decides how; docs/widgets.md says exactly this about glyph glow).
Performance is preserved: retained terminal textures and damage tracking stay as they are. Drawing
terminal cells as ordinary scene commands is REJECTED — cell glyphs are the hottest path in the app.

═══ DOCS (mandatory, same change) ═══
docs/widgets.md gets the new scene command and the content trait, with a native AND a declarative
example for each; AGENTS.md gets the chrome/<kind>/ structure beside the existing expose example and
its stale DrawCommand line fixed. Do NOT create new doc files (Antonio, 2026-08-17).

═══ VERIFICATION ═══
Rendering, layering and input. Green tests are not verification: Antonio drives every visual check.

═══ RELATIONSHIP TO EXISTING WORK ═══
- P089(F011) "The pane header and the info bar come out of chrome/mod.rs" is SWALLOWED by this phase
  (its work becomes chrome/terminal/terminal_header.rs). Fold or mark superseded.
- P082(F003)/T447 "The pane owns its letter" is the letter half of T451 here. Decide whether T447
  ships first as a narrow fix or folds in.

tasks.title: Step 1 — a component can host content something else rasterizes
tasks.description:
═══ PRE-FLIGHT (AGENTS.md § 0 — written 2026-08-19, before any code) ═══

1. WHICH EXISTING THING DOES THIS? The precedent is `Text`, exactly.
   - `DrawCommand` (heca-grid-ui/src/scene.rs, 631 lines) — six variants: Rect, Brackets, Text,
     Scanline, PushClip, PopClip. `TextCmd` (:379) is the model to copy: the scene names a **role**
     and the renderer resolves it ("which family that is lives here, so no widget knows a font's
     name" — heca-renderer/src/scene.rs:145). A surface command is the same bargain with a texture.
   - `enqueue_scene` (heca-renderer/src/scene.rs:92, 318 lines) is one `match cmd` with an arm per
     variant, over a clip stack that intersects nested `PushClip`s and scissors both renderers.
   - The blit already exists and must be REUSED, not rewritten: `blit_retained_terminal_layer`
     (heca/src/app/terminal_render.rs:292) draws `state.terminal_layers[pane_id]` through
     `state.backdrop.draw(..)` at `mount.content_rect`, scaled by `scale_factor`, with an optional
     stencil.

2. WHICH TASK COVERS IT? This one — P094(F011)/T448.

3. ⚠️ WHAT IS NEITHER — the design question this task must answer, found in the pre-flight:

   **`enqueue_scene` cannot do the blit.** Its signature is
   `(grid: &mut GridRenderer, text: &mut TextRenderer, scene: &Scene, glow_alpha_scale: f32)` — it
   feeds two renderers and has NO `wgpu::CommandEncoder` and no target view. The terminal blit needs
   both (`blit_retained_terminal_layer(state, pane_id, encoder, target, viewport_px, mount,
   stencil)`), and it happens in the GPU pass, not while the scene is being enqueued.

   So a new `DrawCommand` cannot be consumed the way the other five are, and there are two ways out:

   (a) **`enqueue_scene` COLLECTS them.** It returns (or fills) the surface placements it walked past
       — `{ id, rect, clip }` — and the host blits each one in its own pass, in scene order, with the
       clip already resolved. The library stays GPU-free and `enqueue_scene` keeps its signature's
       spirit: it still only turns a scene into draw work, and the caller owns the encoder.
   (b) **Give `enqueue_scene` the encoder and target.** Simpler to read at the call site, but it puts
       GPU-pass ownership inside a function that currently has none, and every caller (the app AND
       the showcase) has to supply them.

   (a) is the better fit and keeps the boundary the crate is built on, but it is a REAL choice about
   heca-renderer's shape — put it to Antonio before building, per § 0 rule 3.

   Ordering is the wrinkle either way: the terminal is drawn UNDER the pane chrome today (the shell
   paints after the terminal so the border is not swallowed). A collected placement has to keep that
   relationship rather than compositing on top.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

STEP 1 of P094. Everything from step 2 onward waits on this — but NOT step 0 (T451), which is the
pane shell and its letter and needs nothing from here. (T451 is DONE.)

THE GAP (verified 2026-08-18): heca-grid-ui/src/scene.rs `DrawCommand` has exactly six variants —
Rect, Brackets, Text, Scanline, PushClip, PopClip. There is NO `Custom` and NO `Gradient`, though
AGENTS.md's catalog line claims both. So a component has no way to say "my content is rasterized by
someone else; here is where it goes", which is why the terminal could never be a widget.

BUILD: one new DrawCommand variant naming an EXTERNALLY-RENDERED SURFACE — an opaque id plus the
rect it occupies. The library stays GPU-free: it emits an id and a rect and knows nothing else. This
is the same split `Text` already has — the scene says "this run of text goes here", heca-renderer
owns the atlas and decides how. docs/widgets.md states the principle for glyph glow: "The halo is a
renderer choice, not a scene one."

- heca-grid-ui: the variant + whatever `PaintCx` method emits it. Nothing about wgpu, textures or
  formats crosses into the library.
- heca-renderer: map the id to the texture it already holds and blit it at that rect, honouring the
  clip stack (PushClip/PopClip) so a surface inside a ScrollRegion clips like anything else.
- Who allocates the ids is the HOST's business, not the library's.

RULE ZERO: write the line a plugin author would type. A plugin that renders its own content into a
texture must be able to place it with one builder on its own widget — no host-private type, no
registry. If the answer needs either, the API is wrong.

ALSO IN THIS TASK: correct the stale AGENTS.md line that lists `Gradient` and `Custom` among the
DrawCommand variants, and document the new variant in docs/widgets.md (§ Scene / DrawCommand /
PaintCx) with both audiences, per the mandatory-docs rule.

VERIFICATION: a headless test asserting the command is emitted with the right rect and clip; the
visual proof comes with step 2.

Only the pre-flight was written, and it is kept in the description because it is the useful part: it establishes that `Text` is the precedent to copy and it found the design question below.

Only the pre-flight was written, and it is kept in the description because it is the useful part: it establishes that `Text` is the precedent to copy and it found the design question below.

⚠️ OPEN QUESTION, FOR ANTONIO, BEFORE ANY CODE: `enqueue_scene` (heca-renderer/src/scene.rs:92) takes `(grid, text, scene, glow_alpha_scale)` — no `wgpu::CommandEncoder`, no target view — so it CANNOT perform the blit the way it consumes the other five commands. Either (a) it collects the surface placements it walked past `{id, rect, clip}` and the host blits them in its own pass, or (b) it is given the encoder and target. WHY IT STOPPED, AND IT WAS NOT ABOUT THIS TASK: F011/P094 was started while F003/P082 was the active phase with T444 part-built. That was wrong — a phase is a unit to finish, and the switch also relocated in-flight P082 work into F011. P094 is parked; see its handoff.

tasks.title: Step 2 — Terminal becomes a component you can put anywhere
tasks.description:
STEP 2 of P094. Depends on step 1 (T448).

Antonio, 2026-08-18: "Terminal should be a reusable component similar to a DOM <terminal/> we can put
in any container in the app, even in a plugin or in a sidebar if we want."

TODAY: the terminal is not a component at all. heca/src/app/terminal_render.rs (1700 lines) renders
cells into retained GPU textures (sync_retained_terminal_layers, render_terminal_layer_update) and
blits them (blit_retained_terminal_layer), with stencil and scissor passes around it, plus
queue_terminal_dynamic_overlays. Its rect is computed by hand — stable_tiled_content_rect /
stable_floating_content_rect / pane_content_rect.

BUILD: heca/src/chrome/terminal/ per AGENTS.md § 0b-bis (mod.rs is the ONLY file that may touch
AppState; model.rs is the session reduced to plain data; testing.rs holds fixtures). The `Terminal`
component:
- is an ordinary Component: it gets bounds, focus, events, hit-testing, clipping and children from
  the framework like every other widget;
- paints ONE command — the externally-rendered surface from step 1 — and nothing else;
- takes its rect FROM THE LAYOUT ENGINE. Delete the hand-computed content rects: the engine gives
  the child its bounds, and the GPU pass reads them.

PRESERVE EXACTLY: retained terminal textures, damage tracking, the row-range merge, and the fact
that terminal cell glyphs carry no glow. Cell glyphs are the hottest path in the app. Drawing them as
ordinary scene commands is REJECTED and must not be attempted.

Also moves here: the per-pane viewport widgets (state.pane_viewport_widgets — the "N lines above"
BadgeButton and the scrollbar). They scroll the TERMINAL's scrollback, so they belong to the terminal,
not to the pane. Per the settled tree the terminal sits inside a ScrollRegion that the content owns.

CHECK: the pointer/keyboard funnel. Today mouse routing for pane content is hand-written in
heca/src/mouse.rs against pane rects; as a component it should receive events through the ordinary
tree dispatch. Run something before claiming either way.

VERIFICATION: Antonio drives. A terminal must look and behave identically — same text, same
selection, same scrollback, no new lag — and must additionally render correctly when mounted
somewhere that is not a pane.

tasks.title: Step 3 — the header belongs to the terminal, not to the pane
tasks.description:
STEP 3 of P094. Depends on step 2 (T449). ABSORBS P089(F011)/T376 and T377.

Antonio, 2026-08-18: "the header is not part of the pane. the badge and header are good for terminal,
maybe not for neovim so they are part of the child inside the pane." And: the buttons "simply
dispatch actions. Actions are dispatchable even from RPC so what's the problem? They stay in the
header but are also in the command palette."

TODAY: heca/src/chrome/pane_header.rs is 1086 lines building a retained per-pane info bar
(state.pane_headers, built by sync_pane_headers at :952) that reads terminal facts — cwd, app name,
process status, git branch/added/modified/deleted. The pane RESERVES its height (title_bar_reserve,
pane_title_top_inset, app/terminal_render.rs:621-652) and it is painted by a direct
header.root.paint(cx) at app/terminal_render.rs:800.

BUILD: heca/src/chrome/terminal/terminal_header.rs — the terminal's own header component, a fixed
child in the terminal's composition:

    Flex
      ├─ terminal_header (fixed)
      └─ ScrollRegion
           └─ Terminal

- The pane stops reserving any height. The content lays out its own bar, so title_bar_reserve /
  pane_title_top_inset go away as pane concerns.
- The bar keeps BOTH halves and both keep dispatching actions: config's PaneSegment
  (Location/AppName/GitBranch/GitStatus) are the terminal's own facts, and PaneAction
  (Split/MoveLeft/MoveRight/Close) are pane-level actions the buttons merely dispatch. A button
  naming an action is the documented chrome-button pattern, not coupling — tooltip and shortcut come
  from ActionShortcuts by action NAME, and the same action stays reachable from a keybinding, the
  palette and RPC.
- Keep pane_action_spec / pane_action_name / action_tooltip as the single source for a button's
  glyph, action, label and tip. Do NOT re-introduce a per-action match in a render loop.
- The button set stays a dynamic vector (pane_header_buttons), which is the documented plugin seam.

═══ AND DELETE THE CHARACTER ARITHMETIC WHILE YOU ARE IN THIS FILE ═══
(From P089/T376, whose stated blocker is now resolved: Label::truncate(Ellipsis) LANDED —
heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/label.rs:136, Ellipsis at :41, and the command palette already uses it at
command_palette.rs:319/:331.)

heca/src/chrome/pane_header.rs:227 guesses the layout engine's answer with two magic numbers:

    let char_w = (font * 0.6).max(1.0);          // "one character is about this wide"
    let per_segment_overhead = font * 2.5;       // icon + gaps + padding + divider
    let estimated = text_chars as f32 * char_w + items.len() as f32 * per_segment_overhead;
    // …then computes overflow_chars and calls truncate_path_left on the location segment

taffy already measures the real advances, the real theme padding and the real gaps. The variable is
literally called `estimated`; it is wrong whenever the font ratio, the theme padding or a size
variant differs, and the failure is silent — the bar truncates too early, or overflows and is hard-
clipped by the per-pane render clip.

REPLACE with: give each segment its box and let the label fit itself. truncate_path_left (:122)
keeps the tail behind a leading ellipsis, which is exactly Ellipsis::Start. So the arithmetic, the
two constants and truncate_path_left all go.

NOTE (settles P089/T376's other half): there is NOTHING to build for the segments. `Tag` is already
multi-segment (.segment / .segment_text / .append_to_segment) and build_pane_info_bar already walks
the configured PaneSegment list chaining .segment_text(text, Some(icon)) into one Tag. The "segment
bar component" P089 proposed already exists and is config-driven via [appearance.pane]
title_segments.

BEHAVIOUR TO PRESERVE (from P089): the header rebuild cadence — chrome_signature and the width
bucketing that stops a window resize thrashing the rebuild — must survive the move. (P089's other
preserved behaviour, per-pane hint-id ranges, is itself stale: hint ids were deleted by F004/P084/T399.)

VERIFICATION: Antonio drives. The bar must look unchanged, every button must still act on the right
pane, tooltips must still show the live keybinding, hiding the bar via config must leave no reserved
gap, and a long path must still ellipsise from the left — now by fitting its box rather than by a
character count. Narrow a pane slowly and watch where it cuts.

tasks.title: Step 0 — the Pane becomes a real component, and it owns the letter (DO THIS FIRST)
tasks.description:
═══ PRE-FLIGHT (AGENTS.md § 0 — written 2026-08-18, before any code) ═══

1. WHICH EXISTING WIDGET / FUNCTION DOES THIS? Nothing here is new.
   - The frame: the grid-ui `Pane` widget through `chrome::apply_pane_frame` (chrome/theme.rs:147),
     which is exactly what paint_terminal_pane_shell already builds.
   - Retention: `chrome::sync_pane_headers` (chrome/pane_header.rs:952) is the pattern to COPY, not
     re-invent — phase 1 gathers per-pane inputs under immutable borrows, phase 2 builds only when a
     content key changed, then lays out, translates and prunes. With it: `RetainedPaneHeader { root,
     key }` (:280) and `pane_header_key` (:629), whose width BUCKETING (avail_w / 16.0) is what stops
     a resize thrashing the rebuild.
   - The letter: `Base::hint` / `hint_style` / `HintPlacement::Center`, drawn by
     `component::paint_child`; collected by `heca_grid_ui::collect_hints`, handed out by
     `chrome::offer_hint_letters` (hint.rs:356), run by `fire_hint`, named by `target_identity`
     (:321) which already prefixes an identity with its surface.
   - The pick: `InteractionIntent::FocusPane { pane_id }` posted as `AppEvent::ChromeIntent` — the
     seam `PaneHeaderCtx.event_proxy` already uses for every header button. NOT `chrome::fires`
     (mod.rs:1344): that stamps a provider SEAT_ARG mount, and a pane is not seated in a chrome region.
   - The surface: `HintSurface::PaneHeader(PaneId)` (hint.rs:243) becomes the pane's.

2. WHICH PLANNER TASK COVERS IT? This one — P094(F011)/T451, absorbing the canceled P082(F003)/T447.

3. WHAT IS NEITHER — one thing, and it is a MOVE, not an invention:
   ⚠️ `pane_key(PaneId) -> String` ALREADY EXISTS TWICE, with two different strings:
     - heca/src/providers/workspaces/mod.rs:681 → "pane:7"          (the sidebar row)
     - heca/src/chrome/expose/pane_card.rs:19   → "expose.pane.7"   (the exposé card)
   The expose one is deliberately its own namespace and stays. The provider one is the identity of
   the pane itself, and the pane must declare the SAME string — Antonio's rule: whoever owns the
   thing declares its identity, anything else showing it is a view. So it moves to a place both the
   provider and chrome/pane/ can see rather than becoming a third copy. Do NOT copy it.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

STEP 0 of P094 — the FIRST task, ahead of everything else. Antonio, 2026-08-18: the pane letter is
broken today and must be fixed early, without a throwaway patch. Absorbs P082(F003)/T447, which is
canceled and folded here. P082(F003)/T445 now waits on THIS task.

⚠️ IT DOES NOT DEPEND ON T448 OR T449. The letter needs a retained, keyed pane tree painted through
paint_child — nothing more. The pane's frame is the EXISTING grid-ui `Pane` widget, so no new scene
command is needed, and the terminal keeps blitting into the same rect exactly as it does today (that
is already the paint order). The only part of this task that needs T449 is "holds one content child
and gives it bounds" — that arrives later, and nothing built here is thrown away.

Antonio: "the only responsibility of the pane is to draw the key hint letter, zoom in/out,
float/unfloat, split/unsplit, remove". And: "terminal should not be responsible to render letters.
They are programs that run inside pane. So pane is the container for every future app."

TODAY: there is no pane component. paint_terminal_pane_shell (app/terminal_render.rs:718) builds a
grid-ui `Pane` FRESH EVERY FRAME inside a paint function, lays it out, writes its bounds, and paints
it with a direct pane.paint(cx). Nothing retained means nothing can carry a letter. Consequently the
pane letters for prefix+q are drawn by a HOST PAINT PASS at app/render.rs:951 — a 48px glyph queued
straight to state.text_renderer, outside the theme, outside the keycap primitive, positioned by hand.

BUILD: heca/src/chrome/pane/ per AGENTS.md § 0b-bis. A retained component, one per pane, rebuilt from
plain data each frame the way chrome::sync_pane_headers already does:
- composes the existing grid-ui `Pane` widget for its frame — frame mode, border, radius and glow
  from the theme and [appearance.pane], as today. Nothing hardcoded;
- carries its identity — .key(pane_key(id)) — and what picking it means, emitted through the seam the
  header buttons already use: AppEvent::ChromeIntent with InteractionIntent::FocusPane { pane_id }.
  The pane learns nothing about the sidebar or the picker;
- HintPlacement::Center on its hint style, so the letter lands centred over the pane, which is where
  it is today and what Antonio expects;
- is painted through heca_grid_ui::paint_child, or the framework cannot draw its letter;
- never computes geometry: zoom, float, split and remove are performed by heca-core/src/layout via
  ActionRegistry handlers. The pane dispatches and reflects state (zoomed / floating / active).

THE HEADER, WHILE T450 IS STILL PENDING (decided 2026-08-18): the pane ADOPTS the existing retained
header tree as a child straight away, rather than leaving two surfaces per pane for the picker to
enumerate. That also fixes the header's own direct-paint problem (app/terminal_render.rs:800) early,
and it is the direction of travel — T450 then MOVES that tree into the terminal's composition.

THEN DELETE:
- the host pass at app/render.rs:951 (~43 lines), but ONLY once the widget is proven on screen;
- the direct paints in app/terminal_render.rs (the pane shell at :783 and the header at :800).

THEN: prefix+q assigns through assign_letters (heca/src/handlers.rs:816) exactly as prefix+/ does —
one mechanism, one look, one assignment rule. The candidate list must carry identities rather than
indices; collect_all_pane_candidates (heca/src/app/selection.rs:41) is pure index today, which is
why splitting a column renumbers every letter after it. The picker already treats "one retained tree
per pane" as a surface (HintSurface::PaneHeader(pane_id), chrome/hint.rs:534, occluded by the pane's
own frame rect) — that surface becomes the pane.

⚠️ AN EARLIER ATTEMPT WAS REVERTED. Declaring the letter on the pane HEADER failed for two reasons,
both still true: the header is painted directly so no letter can draw there, and it is a thin strip
so the letter would be in the wrong place. Restore-first if you break it:
git checkout -- heca/src/app/render.rs heca/src/chrome/pane_header.rs

VERIFICATION: rendering. Antonio drives: prefix+q and prefix+/ with the sidebars shown AND hidden,
letters centred over panes, split a pane and check the others keep their letters, zoom in and out.

**Completion summary:**
DONE 2026-08-19, verified on screen by Antonio ("works fine"). Not committed — the working tree carries it.

WHAT SHIPPED
- heca/src/chrome/pane/ — the pane shell as a retained component, per AGENTS.md § 0b-bis: mod.rs (the
  only file touching AppState; `sync_panes` copies the two-phase gather/build/position/prune of
  `sync_pane_headers`), model.rs (`PaneShellModel`), shell.rs (`PaneShell`, `PaneCallbacks`,
  `size_to`), testing.rs. Five headless tests.
- `.key(pane_key(id))` + `KeyHint` with `HintPlacement::Center` + `on_hint` emitting
  `InteractionIntent::FocusPane`. Painted through `heca_grid_ui::paint_child`, which is what draws
  the letter; the pane header's direct paint went through it too.
- `pane_key` now has ONE home (heca/src/chrome/mod.rs); providers/workspaces imports it.
- `HintSurface::Pane(PaneId)` — the pane is its own hint surface, sharing the header's occluder.
- app/render.rs: the 48px host letter pass DELETED (44 lines, incl. its float loop).
- All five pane pick modes assign through `assign_letters` (handlers.rs
  `pane_candidates_with_stable_letters`) — one rule for both pickers, which fixes the k→j report.

BUGS FOUND AND FIXED WHILE DRIVING (all by Antonio on screen; none by the suite)
1. Frame kept the size it was FIRST built at — traced live as asked 648 wide, got 380, every frame.
   Cause: `Px(w)` baked into `build` while the rect was deliberately kept out of the rebuild key.
   Fix: the rect is a per-frame input via `shell::size_to`, shared by the host AND the tests, so a
   test cannot pass while the real placement is wrong. The box test was `<=` (a short border passed
   it) and is now exact, plus a resize-without-rebuild regression test.
2. Inactive pane's letter unreadable: the pane is painted with a theme whose `accent` is overwritten
   with that pane's border colour. The keycap is a picker affordance, so the model carries the real
   theme accent and `KeyHint::color` uses it.
3. Sidebar cap centred under prefix+q, right-aligned under prefix+/. Cause: `offer_hint_by_key`
   labelled the nearest ACTIONABLE node inside the keyed node (the row, default TopCenter) instead of
   the wrapper that DECLARED the pick (CenterRight). Fixed in heca-grid-ui/src/hint.rs by applying
   T441's settled precedence — a declaration outranks mere actionability, in both directions — with
   two regression tests. NB the existing `enclosing` was being overwritten by the keyed node itself,
   so a separate `declaring` ancestor is tracked.
4. A pane scrolled behind a sidebar drew its keycap on top of the sidebar (caps paint on the overlay
   layer, escaping the base clip). Fixed by `chrome::hint::visible_pane_targets`, which ASKS
   `active_hint_targets`/`resolve_hint_layers` — occlusion stays decided in one place. ⚠️ First
   attempt filtered the CANDIDATE, which removed the letter from every view including the sidebar row
   and made the pane unreachable; the occlusion is a fact about a VIEW, so it filters which pane
   shell is handed the letter.
5. Shift cancelled a picker, and capitals were unreachable. `typed_candidate_char` folded to
   lowercase; every pick handler reset the mode on the first key of any kind. Fixed centrally:
   `InputMode::awaits_pick_letter()` (app_state.rs) names the family, ONE guard at the dispatch in
   app/input.rs, ONE `is_modifier_key` on the logical key — which absorbed a pre-existing inline copy
   in the same file. (I first wrote the guard into three of seven handlers; Antonio caught it.)
6. Pane-header buttons changed letters on zoom: they used the DERIVED identity, which moves when the
   content does. Fixed with `.key(spec.action_name)` on the declaring wrapper — unique across panes
   without the pane id, because each header is its own surface (`pane-header:7/zoom`).

DEVIATIONS FROM THE TASK AS WRITTEN
- The pane does NOT adopt the header tree as a child. Re-parenting would move the header (it is
  positioned independently, centred in a reserved band) and the task requires pixel-identical output;
  T450 moves it into the terminal's composition anyway. Both are surfaces under one shared occluder —
  same machinery, one collection, no second path.
- The pick's `InteractionSource` is `Keyboard`, not `MouseContent`: a pick carries no pointer. Left

NOT DONE HERE, RECORDED ELSEWHERE

tasks.title: Step 5 — one trait every pane content implements, and an action picks which one
tasks.description:
STEP 5 of P094. Depends on step 4.

Antonio, 2026-08-18: chrome/terminal, chrome/browser, chrome/neovim "all adhere to a common trait to
stay in a pane. Plugin authors should be able to create other panes and use the components."

TWO SEAMS, DO NOT CONFLATE THEM:
- PaneBackend (heca-core/src/backend/mod.rs:187) is the PROCESS/IO side — bytes, resize, exit. It
  exists, with terminal and fake implementations.
- This task builds the UI side: what can sit inside a pane and be drawn. A terminal implements both
  halves, through different types.

BUILD:
1. The trait. What a pane needs from its content and NOTHING more — the content builds its own tree
   (its header, its ScrollRegion, whatever it composes) and the pane gives it bounds. Apply RULE
   ZERO: a plugin author must be able to implement it from outside this crate with no host-private
   type in any signature. If the trait needs one, the trait is wrong.
2. PaneKind. It does not exist anywhere in the code today. AGENTS.md specifies the target shape:
   SpawnPane { kind: PaneKind, program, argv, float, width, height } with terminal | browser |
   nvim_gui, and a mock/placeholder fallback where a backend is not implemented yet.
3. Wire the action so dispatching it adds a pane of that kind into the scrolling area. Follow the
   "Adding New Actions" checklist end to end: WmAction variant -> build_action() (it is
   parameterized, so it does NOT belong in action_from_name) -> action_priority -> handler ->
   build_registry -> declared args in ActionRegistry::ALL -> action_policy classification -> RPC
   parser -> defaults in keybindings.default.toml/config.default.toml -> README.
   An action with a required argument gets no default binding.
4. Persistence: the session must restore a pane to the right kind. Check what heca-core's
   PaneRuntime and the session snapshot already carry before adding a field.

VERIFICATION: dispatching the action from a keybinding, from the command palette and over RPC all
produce the same pane. Antonio drives the visual half.

tasks.title: Step 6 — a floating pane is the same component, not a second path
tasks.description:
STEP 6 of P094. Depends on step 4.

paint_terminal_pane_shell is called from TWO sites — heca/src/app/render.rs:691 (tiled) and :902
(floating) — and the floating path additionally has its own blur capture, its own stencil and its own
backdrop pass (see the render order documented in AGENTS.md: floating blur capture -> floating
stencil -> floating backdrop + content). heca-core keeps floating panes in a separate list
(Workspace::floating_panes) with their own position/size, and the letter pass in render.rs:951 has a
SECOND loop just for them.

The PRIMARY RULE is one path: two paths over one input cannot stay identical, and nothing fails when
they drift — the tests exercise one and the user sees the other.

BUILD: a floating pane mounts the SAME pane component from step 4, given a different rect and told it
is floating. Its extra GPU passes stay in the renderer where they belong; they are how it is
rasterized, not a different kind of pane. The floating-specific letter loop in render.rs goes with the
rest of that pass.

WATCH: ActionPolicy::Floating already restricts which actions are allowed while a floating pane is
active (only FocusedPaneLocal + Global). The pane component dispatches actions; it must not
second-guess that policy with a check of its own — the router answers it.

VERIFICATION: Antonio drives. Float a pane (prefix+f), check the frame, the blur, the header and the
letter; pick it with prefix+q and prefix+/; unfloat and check it returns to its slot.

tasks.title: Step 7 — a second content kind, so the trait is not terminal-shaped
tasks.description:
STEP 7 of P094. Depends on step 5. This is the task that proves the phase.

A trait with one implementation is a description of that implementation. Everything above is designed
so a second content kind costs one folder and nothing else — this task collects on that, and it is
where a wrong assumption shows up while it is still cheap.

BUILD the smallest second content that is genuinely NOT a terminal, in heca/src/chrome/<kind>/
per AGENTS.md § 0b-bis. Deliberately choose one whose shape differs on the axes that matter:
- NO header at all (Antonio: the header is "not in neovim") — proving the pane reserves nothing and
  the content owns its own layout;
- content drawn as ORDINARY WIDGETS (Flex / Grid / ScrollRegion / Label / Button), not through the
  externally-rendered surface from step 1 — proving the pane's content child works both ways, which
  is the phase's central design call;
- its own scrolling, inside its own ScrollRegion — proving the pane bounds and the content scrolls.

An agent panel or a browser placeholder both fit; pick with Antonio.

THEN: mount the SAME component somewhere that is not a pane — a sidebar dock — and check it renders.
That is the claim the whole phase rests on ("we can put it in any container in the app, even in a
plugin or in a sidebar"), and it is either true or it is not.

FINALLY: write it up. docs/widgets.md gets the content trait and both content examples with a native
AND a declarative form, per the mandatory-docs rule; AGENTS.md gets the chrome/<kind>/ structure
beside the existing expose example. Do NOT create a new doc file (Antonio, 2026-08-17).

VERIFICATION: Antonio drives. Two kinds of pane side by side in one column, both pickable by
prefix+/, both zoomable and floatable, and the second kind also mounted in a sidebar.

tasks.title: Step 4b — a click finds its pane through the tree, not a hand-written hit test
tasks.description:
STEP 4b of P094. Runs with step 4 (T451) — once the pane is a real component, this is what makes it
worth being one. Sibling of P082(F003)/T446, which does the same for the chrome.

TODAY (heca/src/mouse/hit_test.rs:17, hit_test_pane_excluding): the app finds the pane under the
cursor by hand. It re-derives the chrome content rect, walks the floating panes and then
panes_with_positions, and compares raw coordinates against each rect — the exact shape AGENTS.md § 0c
forbids ("a widget never hit-tests"; "if you are writing bounds.contains(pos), stop"). It also
carries a hardcoded 40.0 fallback for the left sidebar width, which is a magic number standing in for
a value the chrome already knows.

That helper is only the entry point: heca/src/mouse.rs is 662 lines and mouse/ is 2644 in total —
target.rs, hit_test.rs, drag.rs, release.rs, interactive.rs, resize.rs all reason about where the
pointer is rather than about what it landed on.

BUILD: once panes are components with real bounds, the pointer already resolves to one. The framework
hit-tests a single Event::Raw(RawPointer) — children before parents, topmost first, clipped subtrees
excluded — so a float over a tiled pane and a zoomed column over the panes behind it come out right
by construction rather than by the order this function happens to test in. A pane answers a click
with a handler and lets what it does not want bubble.

DELETE what the tree makes redundant: hit_test_pane / hit_test_pane_excluding and the coordinate
arithmetic that feeds them, plus that 40.0.

DO NOT DELETE what is genuinely geometric: interactive move and edge resize track a drag against
layout rects and belong to the WM, not to a widget's bounds. Decide each call site on evidence, one
at a time.

⚠️ VERIFY BY RUNNING, NOT BY GREPPING. heca-grid-ui/tests/click_to_focus_by_handler.rs already proves
the bubbling half for chrome rows; the drag framework's resolve_at/source_at read the same bounds.
Add the equivalent for panes before changing any call site, and check the funnel test
(heca/tests/pointer_funnel.rs) still passes — a host that delivers presses without releases produces
no clicks at all.

VERIFICATION: Antonio drives. Click a pane to focus it; click a float over a tiled pane; click a
zoomed pane; drag a pane; resize by its edge; right-click for the context menu; and check
focus_follows_mouse still behaves.

tasks.title: Step 3b — the sidebar's git branch fits its box instead of a hardcoded 22 characters
tasks.description:
STEP 3b of P094. The last of P089(F011)/T376's four hand-rolled truncations, and the only one that is
not a pane concern — it belongs to the SIDEBAR, which is why it needs its own task rather than riding
along with the terminal header (T450).

TODAY:
- heca/src/chrome/mod.rs:412 — `const SIDEBAR_GIT_BRANCH_MAX_CHARS: usize = 22;`
- heca/src/chrome/mod.rs:416 — `truncate_sidebar_git_branch(branch)` = truncate_path_left(branch, 22)
- heca/src/chrome/signals.rs:342 — computes `branch_display` and writes it into a SECOND signal
  (`sigs.git_branch_display`) sitting beside the real one (`sigs.git_branch`). Two signals for one
  string, kept in step by hand.

WHY IT GOES: 22 is a fixed character cap that ignores how much room the row actually has, so the
sidebar truncates even when there is space, and does not truncate when there is not (a narrow
sidebar still gets 22 characters). Label::truncate(Ellipsis::Start) does exactly what
truncate_path_left does — keep the tail behind a leading ellipsis — and fits the real box, measured
by the layout engine.

BUILD: give the branch label its box, call .truncate(Ellipsis::Start), and delete
SIDEBAR_GIT_BRANCH_MAX_CHARS, truncate_sidebar_git_branch, the git_branch_display signal and the
bookkeeping in signals.rs that keeps it in step. Check whether truncate_path_left has any caller left
after T450; if not, it goes too.

⚠️ A shrinkable label needs BOTH halves or the cut is unreachable: the paint-time cut AND declaring
the label shrinkable (flex_shrink + min_width: 0). Without the second the engine never hands it less
than its natural width. This is recorded from P091/T379, where it was found the hard way.

VERIFICATION: Antonio drives. A long branch name in the sidebar at several sidebar widths — it must
ellipsise from the left and must now use the room it has, which is a VISIBLE change from today's
fixed 22-character cut.

tasks.title: Step 8 — one picker, not seven: a picker is a widget, and InputMode stops naming entities
tasks.description:
STEP 8 of P094. Decided with Antonio, 2026-08-18, from the question that exposed it: "I see hardcoded
InputMode. What if a plugin want to show and select some other entity? How do they do?"

They cannot. That is the defect.

═══ THE DEFECT ═══

`InputMode` (heca/src/app_state.rs) is a CLOSED ENUM IN THE CORE, and its pick variants NAME THE
ENTITY TYPE:

    InputMode::PaneSelect  { candidates: Vec<(char, PaneId)> }
    InputMode::PaneSwap    { candidates: Vec<(char, PaneId)>, focus_after: bool }
    InputMode::PaneTake    { candidates: Vec<(char, PaneId)>, focus_after: bool }
    InputMode::WorkspacePick { candidates: Vec<(char, usize)>, target: … }
    InputMode::ColumnPick  { candidates: Vec<(char, usize, usize)> }
    InputMode::FollowLink  { candidates: Vec<LinkHint> }
    InputMode::HintPick    { candidates: Vec<(char, HintTarget)> }

A plugin cannot add a variant, cannot build any of those candidate lists, and so cannot have the host
letter its containers, its files, its git hunks. **There is no line a plugin author could write.**
⭐⭐ RULE ZERO. No filter or argument fixes it — the shape is closed by construction.

Each variant also drags its own handler (handle_pane_select_mode, handle_pane_swap_mode,
handle_pane_take_mode, handle_follow_link_mode, handle_hint_pick_mode, + the workspace/column ones,
all in heca/src/app/input.rs), each re-implementing "match the typed letter, end the mode". Seven
copies of one rule — which is how the modifier guard came to be missing from four of them
(F011/P094/T451, 2026-08-18).

═══ THE ANSWER: A PICKER IS A WIDGET, AND IT ALREADY EXISTS ═══

    let open = signal(false);                 // flipped from an action
    KeyHintGroup::new(my_subtree).open_when(open)

That is the whole thing. The group holds focus while open — and holding focus IS taking the keyboard,
so there is no mode to enter, no gate to write and nothing the host must be told. It letters its own
descendants, claims the typed letter in the CAPTURE phase before the subtree sees it, and runs the
picked widget's own declaration. **The entity is never named in the core, because the picker letters
WIDGETS, not entities** — a plugin's Docker container is just a row that declared what picking it
does.

The exposé already works exactly this way and proves it: it declares `heca.expose.pick`, config binds
`[[keys.surface]] pick = "s"`, and `s` letters its cards only. There is no `InputMode::ExposePick`.

So `InputMode`'s pick variants are the LEGACY: they predate KeyHintGroup. The destination is that
every picker is a KeyHintGroup — a component's, a plugin's, and the core's, where `prefix+/` is that
widget at surface scope and `prefix+q` is the same with an eligibility filter.
docs/hint-architecture.md § 2c already says this in as many words.

═══ WHAT `prefix+q` VS `prefix+/` COSTS TODAY ═══
They are two implementations of one gesture, differing at every step:

| | prefix+/ (HintPick) | prefix+q (PaneSelect) |
| candidate is | a WIDGET (HintTarget{surface,path}) | a DOMAIN ID (PaneId) |
| targets found by | collect_hints, walking the laid-out tree | collect_all_pane_candidates, walking the SESSION |
| letter delivered by | offer_hint(root, &path, label) — BY PATH | offer_hint_by_key(root, key, label) — BY KEY STRING |
| what a pick does | fire_hint runs THE WIDGET'S declaration | the handler dispatches WmAction::FocusPane itself (input.rs:565) |

Row 3 is why the sidebar keycap is right-aligned under `prefix+/` and centred under `prefix+q`
(Antonio, driving, 2026-08-18): by-path lands on the widget that DECLARED the pick (the row's KeyHint
wrapper, carrying CenterRight); by-key lands on whatever node carries that key, with the default
placement. Same letter, two widgets, two looks. Neither placement is wrong.
Row 4 is why a plugin's pane could never join `prefix+q` however correctly it used the API: it is
never asked.

═══ WHAT TO BUILD ═══
1. `prefix+q` becomes the hint picker with an eligibility filter, not a mode. Its letters already come
   from the shared `assign_letters` (T451); this is the rest.
2. The picker's continuation is the caller's. Swap / take / move-to-column / move-to-workspace are
   "pick a target, THEN do X with it" — one picker that yields the chosen target, not five modes.
3. Delete: the InputMode pick variants and their handlers; collect_all_pane_candidates /
   collect_workspace_candidates / collect_column_candidates (heca/src/app/selection.rs);
   `offer_hint_by_key` + `offer_in_every_tree` + `wanted` (heca/src/chrome/hint.rs) — every target is
   then addressed the one way, by where it is in the tree, and the library stops having two doors for
   handing a widget its letter.
4. `InputMode::awaits_pick_letter` (app_state.rs:201) goes with them — the family it names stops
   existing.

═══ DEPENDENCIES — VERIFIED, AND NARROWER THAN FIRST CLAIMED ═══
- **T436 (P082/F003)** is the real prerequisite for the plugin half: KeyHintGroup has no `WidgetKind`
  and `on_action` has no declarative form, so a plugin can BE PICKED but cannot OWN A PICKER.
- **T432 (P082/F003)** is needed only for the GENERAL filter ("letter every target whose pick does
  X") and for dropping picks the policy would refuse — both need the pick to carry an `Intent`
  instead of an opaque `Box<dyn Fn()>`.
- **NEITHER is needed to fold `prefix+q` into the hint picker for panes**: a surface filter over the
  `HintSurface::Pane` added by T451 expresses "only panes" today, with no string parsing. Caveat: the
  sidebar row showing that pane lives in the Chrome surface, so a surface filter alone would not
  letter it — decide whether that is wanted before choosing.

═══ ALSO SETTLE HERE ═══
The pick's `InteractionSource`. T451 labels a pane pick `Keyboard` rather than `MouseContent`, on the
grounds that a pick carries no pointer (the same reasoning already applied to Rpc). It changes
behaviour in exactly one case — with a dock focused the domain becomes `Container`, so the pick is
allowed where `MouseContent` would resolve to `Floating` and refuse. NOT established by tracing: a
pick and a real click emitted the same source before that change, so no trace can separate them.

═══ VERIFICATION ═══
Antonio drives. `prefix+q` and `prefix+/` must be indistinguishable in look and placement, on panes
and on sidebar rows alike; swap/take must still work; and a second content kind (T454) must be
pickable by a picker it declares itself, with nothing added to the core.

text, reports mouse to the PTY, scrolls its scrollback and answers `prefix+/`. If placing a component
requires the host to teach it anything, the component is not finished.

## THE DECISION T448 WAS WAITING ON — NOW MADE

`enqueue_scene` (`heca-renderer/src/scene.rs:92`) takes `(grid, text, scene, glow_alpha_scale)` — no
GPU encoder, no target view — so a component cannot hand it externally-rasterised content the way the
other five commands are consumed. Antonio delegated the choice (2026-08-28: *"Its up to you to decide
the best way to do it"*), and **(a) is chosen**:

**(a) The scene collects PLACEMENTS `{id, rect, clip}`; the host does the GPU work.** A component
says *"my picture belongs in this box, clipped to this"* and touches no GPU machinery. The host walks
those placements in its own pass afterwards.

- **Single responsibility** — the scene builder describes *what* to draw; an encoder would give it a
  second job, owning GPU pass lifetime.
- **Reusability** — the showcase uses the same builder and has no GPU pass of its own. Under (b)
  every caller must supply an encoder and target.
- **Plugin-friendly / Rule Zero** — (b) drags `wgpu` types across the crate boundary. A plugin
  composing a tree containing a terminal must never see one.
- **Dependency inversion** — `heca-grid-ui` stays GPU-free; the host depends on the placement
  abstraction, not the reverse.

**It is NOT a terminal feature.** The seam is *"a component hosting content something else
rasterises"*, so an image surface, a video pane and a plugin's own canvas get it for free.

⚠️ Ordering must survive: the terminal is drawn **under** the pane chrome today (the shell paints
after it so the border is not swallowed). A collected placement has to preserve that.

## WHERE THE TERMINAL LIVES — the widget/component split

- **`heca-grid-ui`** — the reusable half: a widget hosting a rasterised surface, owning its scroll
  region, its selection gestures and its hit-testing. It binds no app concept, so by AGENTS § 0b it
  belongs in the library.
- **`heca/src/components/terminal/`** — `Terminal` itself, binding the PTY and the backend session.
  Folder structure as agreed: `mod.rs` the only file that may touch `AppState`, `model.rs` the
  session reduced to plain data, `testing.rs` for fixtures. Straight into `components/`, not beside a
  surface — the point is that it is tied to none.

**PRESERVE EXACTLY** (from T449): retained terminal textures, damage tracking, the row-range merge,
and the fact that terminal cell glyphs carry no glow. Cell glyphs are the hottest path in the app;
drawing them as ordinary scene commands is REJECTED and must not be attempted.

## Recent decisions

- **The scene seam is (a): the scene collects placements, the host does the GPU work.** Chosen for
  single responsibility, reusability in the showcase, and keeping `wgpu` out of the crate boundary.
- **The seam is generic** — "a component hosting content something else rasterises", not a terminal
  feature.
- **The terminal splits along the widget/component line** — the surface-hosting widget in
  `heca-grid-ui`, `Terminal` in `heca/src/components/terminal/`.
- **P097 is a prerequisite, not an overlap.** `P097/T498` canceled in favour of this phase's T449.
- **T458 is DONE** (2026-08-28, verified on screen) — the positional `ws:`/`col:` ancestor keys this
  phase exposed. A sidebar row keeps its letter, cursor, right-click target and drag identity across
  a split, and `ColumnId` became a real allocated id rather than a number derived from the column
  count.
- **T457** still needs `F003/P082/T436` (a plugin can own a picker) and `T432` for its plugin half.
